blanks.sentence: A person may enjoy books but still read on screens most days because of the availability of _____.
blanks.section: NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS — Why screens are common

blanks.sentence: Among the qualities reading may bring are creativity, intelligence and _____.
Reading for enjoyment is one factor linked to children becoming _____ later in life.
Researchers have found that children's deep-reading skills develop better when they read from _____.
Deep reading uses more of the _____ than reading at a surface level.
A high volume of material can increase the tendency towards _____.
Reading on screens tends to encourage a _____ understanding, focused on what is easy to grasp.
The heavy flow of words comes with pings and _____.

multipleChoice.question: What tension does the opening discussion illustrate?
options: Enjoying books can lead someone to avoid digital reading most days.
Enjoying books can coexist with frequent reading from screens.
Frequent screen use shows that printed books have lost their appeal.
Frequent screen use is mainly a deliberate choice to protect one's eyes.

multipleChoice.question: What is the main point of Cowell's comments about reading?
options: Its chief benefit is to make children better at school examinations.
Its value lies chiefly in replacing other forms of entertainment.
Its benefits are limited to creativity and intelligence in childhood.
It may support personal qualities and later-life advantages.

multipleChoice.question: Why does the discussion distinguish deep reading from reading in general?
options: Some of reading's benefits depend on understanding meaning beyond the surface.
Children can read deeply only after learning about digital information.
Deep reading is mainly a way of increasing the number of words read.
General reading is valuable only when it leads to economic success.

multipleChoice.question: According to Wolf, what separates deep reading from surface reading?
options: Deep reading gathers information more quickly than surface reading.
Deep reading depends on knowing the author's intended answer.
Deep reading engages more mental processes to interpret the text.
Deep reading reduces the need to make judgments about the text.

multipleChoice.question: Which view best reflects Wolf's point about the amount people read?
options: The volume matters most because it shows whether readers are literate.
The way people read matters more, while high volume may encourage skimming.
The subject matters most because some texts contain fewer distractions.
The amount matters less only when the material is read from books.

multipleChoice.question: What contrast does the discussion draw between screens and books?
options: Screens tend to encourage surface reading; books can support deeper interpretation.
Screens prevent all critical thought; books guarantee it in every reader.
Screens mainly develop empathy; books mainly provide quick factual information.
Screens and books develop the same skills when readers use them for equal periods.

multipleChoice.question: How does the discussion explain why screens can discourage deep reading?
options: Their physical light makes readers forget the meaning of words.
Their information arrives too slowly for readers to stay engaged.
Their text lacks the comparisons needed for careful interpretation.
Their large flow of words and alerts encourages rapid overview reading.
